newsitem.title: TURKEY: Blast rocks smouldering Turkish tanker.
newsitem.headline: Blast rocks smouldering Turkish tanker.

text.p: A new explosion rocked Turkey's biggest oil tanker as it smouldered in Istanbul's Tuzla dockyard on Friday after a fire that blazed all night and dockyard officials said the 20-year-old tanker may face the scrap.
Private NTV news television channel showed the latest explosion in a live broadcast. The tanker was engulfed in white clouds of smoke after the blast.

The state-run Anatolian news agency said a fireboat involved in putting out the fire had been smothered by smoke and flames after the explosion. The boat, the Sonduren, had to be pulled away from the blazing tanker.
It was unclear if there were any casualties in the new explosion.
"The fire is still continuing but it has been under control since the morning," said one dockyard official earlier.
"At this stage we cannot say anything as to when the fire can be put out completely," he told Reuters.

Environment Minister Ziyattin Tokar told Anatolian at the site that 27 people, 19 of them firemen, were injured in the fire, which erupted on the 159,982-tonne TPAO-Istanbul after an explosion at 1530 GMT on Thursday.
Officials said the firemen were injured when they got on the deck of the tanker, presuming the fire was dying out.
"The inexperience of the firemen worsened the casualties," Tokar said.
He said three fireboats were being used to put out the fire and cool the tanker and they had 18 tonnes of foam ready for use in case the fire spread.
Officials earlier said the tanker was empty, but Tokar said it was carrying 500 tonnes of fuel-oil and 35 tonnes of diesel petrol, and some of its cargo was spilling into the sea.
"We will use equipment to cleanse the sea," he said.
Officials said two bulk carriers anchored on the sides of the tanker were towed away after the fire broke out.
The TPAO-Istanbul was Turkey's biggest oil tanker, built in 1977 and owned by state maritime company Ditas. It was in the yard for repairs for eight days.
"I do not think the tanker can be used again. I think it will be scrapped," the dockyard official said.
Witnesses said they heard a few small explosions in the morning but officials did not confirm this.
Officials said explosions in the gas depot were responsible for the fire, but the reason for the blasts was unclear.
